{"class": "fixable",
 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "async I/O page read of orders table B-tree",
                 "component": "asynchronous I/O layer",
                 "frozen": true,
                 "why_every_version_executes_it": "A full scan for LIKE '%qz%' cannot use an index, so every orders page must pass through the frozen I/O layer.",
                 "least_work": {"amount": 4394,
                                "unit": "pages",
                                "per_unit_cost_us": 1.0,
                                "total_ms": 4.4,
                                "calling_context": "warm OS cache, batched reads; first statement only, others assumed similar or cheaper"},
                 "max_cores": 4}],
 "floor_ms": 4.4,
 "L_delta": -4.02,
 "rationale": "Turso's time goes to exec_like, about 61% of 3.7G instructions. That is VDBE code, which the contract leaves mutable. Rewriting it as a precompiled substring search (memchr/memmem for '%x%' patterns, no per-row pattern work) would cut it to roughly SQLite's ~30% share and bring Turso within the band. The 4.4 ms floor is my estimate of frozen I/O work, assuming ~1 µs per page; it is negligible against the 245.9 ms reference upper bound. The 4 ms start-up difference is minor."}
